 "score_claims": "Team V.exe, official practice scores in submission order: 2.56 (v0), 3.44 (v1), 3.58 (v2), 3.81 (v3, best, commit 293eefc), 3.50 (v4), 3.81 (v6), 3.04 (v7), 3.79 (v8), 3.75 (v3 with only the RNG salt changed). Decision time p99 about 5 ms in Python 3.13 + numpy/scipy.",
 "architecture": "Single Python file of about 600 lines plus a raster world model and a waypoint-graph navigator; no state machine object and no utility scoring for movement. Each decision runs four layers in order: (1) bookkeeping (damage memory, sound memory 3 s, per-enemy last-seen table, \"hostile\" timestamps, stuck timer, free-for-all evidence counter); (2) target choice by an additive cost; (3) aim and fire per weapon; (4) movement from a fixed priority cascade: zone danger > combat (recover-to-cover / retreat, else range keeping and strafing, or path to a hidden target) > walk to a better weapon > walk to a cube within 70 m > stance for shooting an NPC or crate > supply drop > drift to a hold point > idle. Two overrides are applied after the cascade: an unstick manoeuvre and a mortar-shell dodge. Movement selection is wrapped so any exception falls back to walking toward the zone centre while firing continues. The only persistent mode flag is \"recovering\". Target cost = distance + 0.04 x enemy HP + 150 if not visible - 40 if it is the current target - 60 (visible) or - 20 (hidden) if it damaged us within 3 s, and a further - 120 if it hit us within the last second and is visible (the v4 addition). Mode split: practice vs free-for-all is inferred at run time by counting drops in the alive count that our own kill events do not explain; one unexplained death switches to free-for-all targeting for the rest of the match (the v6 branch variant: only if it happens before 90 s, or after 3 in total). Heavy precomputation (world rasters, nav graph) is done at Docker image build time and loaded from a cache.",
 "navigation": "Ground only. The map is rasterised onto the 1 m terrain grid: per cell the lowest base and highest top of buildings and, separately, bridges. A cell blocks walking if a prism rises more than the step height above ground and its base is below mech height (so high bridges can be walked under), or if the terrain gradient exceeds the 50 degree slope; the blocked mask is dilated by 3.2 m (base radius plus margin) and a 3-cell border is closed. A waypoint graph on an 8 m lattice (each node snapped to the nearest walkable cell within about 4 m) links neighbours in 16 directions (offsets up to 2 lattice steps with coprime components) when the straight segment is walkable. At run time it computes a whole-graph shortest-path field per goal node with scipy and caches about 25 goals. Steering: if the goal is under 80 m and straight-line walkable, go straight; otherwise pick, among the 8 cheapest nodes within 24 m (distance to node plus field cost), the first that is straight-line walkable, then look up to 5 nodes further along the path for the farthest one still reachable in a straight line. No roof, jet or jump use in normal movement; if it finds itself more than 2.5 m above ground it simply walks straight at the goal. Stuck handling: when commanding movement but moving under 1.5 m/s for about 0.8 s accumulated, it spends 1.2 s moving in a random direction 0.6-1.6 rad off the previous heading with jump and boost held. Boost is otherwise used only outside the zone or within 3 m of its edge, when retreating, when more than 6 m from a cover point, when more than 60 m from a supply drop, and when dodging a shell. Strafing is reversed when the point 4 m ahead is not walkable.",
 "aiming_and_fire_control": "Aim point is the body centre (4.5 m scaled by cubes). Gun: linear lead from the observed velocity, three fixed-point iterations on flight time, vertical velocity clamped to +/-6 m/s and half-weighted; fires whenever ammo is loaded, the target is within the weapon's stat range (about 230 m) and the current aim is inside a distance-scaled window: yaw error under atan(0.75 x target radius / distance) and pitch error under atan(0.35 x target height / distance), each plus 4 mrad. Laser: aimed directly (no lead); starts charging as soon as cooldown is over and a mech or NPC (never a crate) is within laser range, keeps holding until the charge is at least 97% of full AND the aim window is satisfied, then releases; if the target disappears it keeps holding and lets the 2 s auto-fire happen. When the laser is ready/charging or lightning is in range, the torso uses the direct aim rather than the gun lead, so the gun only fires if its lead solution happens to still be within tolerance. Lightning: fires when the target is within 97% of range, energy is at least shot cost + 2, and yaw error is under 45% of the cone angle. Mortar: mechs only, 30-220 m, low-arc ballistic solution with no target lead (launch point taken 9.5 m above the feet, target shortened 3 m and lowered 3 m), fired when yaw and pitch are within 0.03 rad; against a known but hidden target it lobs the high arc at the remembered position. Line of fire is tested by sampling the ray every 1 m against the rasters (to body centre or to a head point); trees are ignored entirely. Reload: only out of combat (no target, no enemy seen within 4 s and 160 m) when the magazine is below half. When nothing is targetable it looks toward the last damage bearing for 2.5 s (explicitly to keep the front arc toward the attacker because rear hits are x1.5), then toward a hidden target, a recently remembered enemy (6 s), the newest near/mid sound, and finally sweeps +/-0.9 rad around the travel direction.",
 "survival_and_anti_squad_tactics": "Core practice-mode idea (v3, their best): do not shoot or approach non-hunters. A mech is \"hostile\" for 12 s if (a) it is within 220 m and its aim yaw is within 0.12 rad of the bearing to us (0.25 rad if it is charging a laser), (b) it damaged us, or (c) we hit it. In practice mode every non-hostile mech farther than 25 m is ignored as a target; in detected free-for-all all mechs are targets. Stated goal: kill each pursuer cheaply, recover behind cover, survive the next one. Recovery cycle (v2): enter when HP < 45%, or when 2+ currently visible enemies are within 120 m and HP < 70%; leave when HP > 85%, or when the target is within 22 m and has less HP than we do. While recovering it searches rings at 7, 12, 18, 25 and 34 m (16 bearings each) for the nearest spot that is walkable, straight-line reachable, at least 5 m inside the zone as it will be 10 s ahead, and hidden from the eye points of up to 4 threats at both body-centre and head height; nearest ring wins with a small bonus for distance from threats; result cached 1 s. It stands still on the spot (\"cover\"), and stands still (\"lurk\") while the target is out of sight. With no cover found it runs 60 m directly away from the target (clamped to 80% of the zone radius) with boost and strafe. v4 disables recovery when only two mechs remain. Fighting stance: preferred range 28 m with lightning and energy above 25, 85 m with a laser, otherwise 60 m, with a +/-15 m band; closes or backs off outside the band and strafes perpendicular, flipping side every 0.8-2.2 s, at full strafe weight when the enemy is charging a laser. A hidden non-recovering target is pursued by pathing to its last position. Incoming mortar shells: predicted landing point within 11 m triggers a boosted move away. No kiting logic on main (the long-range backpedal variant, v7, was rejected), no explicit handling of the single early hunter versus the late all-hunt phase, no jump or roof use for escape.",
 "loot_weapons_upgrades": "Fixed weapon ranking: laser 3.0 > lightning 2.5 > gun 2.0 > mortar 1.0. A floor weapon is wanted only if it beats the worst held one, so the end loadout is laser + lightning and the starting gun is discarded once both are found. Pickup value = rank gain x 100 minus distance; search radius 160 m while a slot is empty (widened from 90 m in v2), 90 m otherwise; the item must be 8 m inside the zone as predicted 10 s ahead; a pickup is blacklisted for 5 s after a failed take; the swap drops the lowest-ranked weapon but never a laser that is mid-charge. Cubes: walk to the nearest one within 70 m that is 10 m inside the upcoming zone. NPC drones: shot when no mech target exists, within 140 m with a clear line; it backs away when closer than 35 m and strafes otherwise. Crates: shot only when no enemy has been seen within 4 s and 160 m, within 90 m with a clear line, standing still. Supply drops: goes only when the drop lands within 15 s, HP is above 40%, the drop is at least 10 m inside the upcoming zone and within 220 m; boosts when over 60 m away and stands still once 2 m inside the ring; no check for contesting mechs. Upgrade choice is a static priority list, independent of the loadout: armor, plating, nanites, laser damage, lightning efficiency, gun damage, gun rate, laser charge, gyros, gun magazine, lightning range, lightning chain, reactor, capacitor, servos, sensors, the three mortar upgrades, jets, gun velocity, laser pierce. They list a loadout-dependent upgrade order as an untried idea.",
 "zone_and_endgame": "Each tick it interpolates the circle now and 10 s ahead. \"Zone danger\" is true when we are outside the zone or farther from the 10-s-ahead centre than its radius minus 8 m; this outranks everything. It then paths to that centre (or to the hold point if already within half the radius), boosting when outside or within 3 m of the edge, and keeps strafing and firing if a target is visible. The idle hold point sits on our side of the next circle at 55% of its radius; it drifts there at 80% speed when more than 12 m away. Cover spots, loot, cubes and drops are all filtered to lie inside the upcoming zone with margins of 5-10 m. The check uses straight-line distance, not path travel time (their own notes say it should compare time left against a walkable route and re-check the final move after the dodge and unstick overrides, since those can undo a safe zone decision). No special handling of the last circles; the only endgame rule is v4's \"no retreat when two mechs remain\", which lowered the practice score.",
 "housebot_observations": "From their rules file and experiments: the practice squad shares sightings, never fights itself, sends the weakest hunter first, adds hunters as we kill them and sends everyone late; non-hunters leave us alone unless we hurt them. Their local squad model encodes this as: number of hunters = 1 + our kills, all hunt after 300 s, hunters ordered easy -> medium -> hard -> expert, hunters know our position while any squad member has seen us within 5 s, non-hunters become active for 6 s after being hurt. Tier parameters in that model (credited to public notes from jklein07's repo, not measured by them): aim error sigma 3.5/2.0/1.3/0.8 degrees for easy/medium/hard/expert resampled every 0.3 s, reaction delay 0.7/0.45/0.3/0.15 s on target switch, lead fraction 0.4/0.75/1.0/1.0, laser error about 2.5 degrees, preferred range about 55 m (25 m with lightning). Official evidence against that model: long-range duelling at 130-160 m lost 0.77, so the real squad is clearly more dangerous at long range than an angular-error model predicts. Identical behaviour gave an identical official score (3.81 twice), which they read as the scorer being deterministic for identical behaviour (fixed match seeds), and as showing that no late unexplained house-bot death occurred in the 48 practice matches (i.e. house bots effectively do not die to zone/NPCs late while we are alive). In the public play server's private rooms the empty seats are house bots playing free-for-all (not the squad), so that server tests final-round play only. Rear-armour hits (x1.5) were observed live.",

  "v3: in practice only engage mechs that shot at us or are aiming at us (plus anything within 25 m): 3.58 -> 3.81 (+0.23). Their sim agreed in direction: practice 1.56 vs 1.19, free-for-all 7.91 vs 7.09.",
  "v4: never retreat when only two mechs remain, and strongly prefer whoever hit us in the last second: 3.81 -> 3.50 (-0.31) on practice, although the sim showed no difference.",
  "v6: making the free-for-all detector stricter (unexplained death counts only before 90 s, or 3+ overall) scored exactly 3.81, identical to v3; paired sim -0.04 +/- 0.04.",
  "v8: closer engagement ranges (gun 40 m, laser 60 m, versus 60 m and 85 m): 3.79 vs 3.81, no effect.",
  "v7: long-range duelling (hold 130 m with gun / 160 m with laser, backpedal while firing): 3.04 vs 3.81 (-0.77), while their sim had predicted +0.3 to +1.0. Rejected; they conclude the sim is not predictive for engagement-range changes.",
  "Noise measurement: the same v3 strategy with only its own RNG salt changed scored 3.75 vs 3.81 (-0.06); they conclude scorer noise is about 0.1 and differences above about 0.15 are real (single sample; elsewhere they still quote +/-0.3 and use a keep-threshold of +0.3).",
  "Not submitted, v5: stay healing in cover until 85% HP. It removed the 'recovery leak' (ticks in recovery without actually regenerating: 932 -> 0) but the paired sim was -0.33 +/- 0.19 (0 wins, 4 losses of 24 matches), so it failed their gate.",
  "Live free-for-all on the real engine: v3 placed 2nd with 4 kills and 14 cubes, then lost the final 1v1 because it kept retreating to cover; v4 died at 44 s in 10th with 1 kill. They note single live matches are very noisy.",
  "Their strategy note: every place is worth the same, so track how often the bot dies first (scores 0), not just the mean; surviving longer but still dying first is worth nothing.",
  "Submission limit they work under: 4 submissions per hour per team."

 "novel_ideas": [
  "Passive-squad rule: classify hunters by behaviour (aim cone on us within 220 m, wider cone if charging; damage dealt to us; mechs we hit) and refuse to engage anyone else in practice mode. Their largest tactical gain (+0.23).",

  "Scorer calibration by experiment: resubmitting the same strategy with a different RNG salt to measure noise, and noticing that behaviourally identical commits get exactly the same score (so resubmitting an unchanged bot will not re-roll the score).",
  "Live harness on the public play server: the bot is run inside the browser (Python compiled to WebAssembly) in private rooms whose empty seats are the server's house bots, giving real-engine free-for-all tests outside the submission quota.",

  "Cover finder: concentric ring sampling up to 34 m, requiring the spot to be hidden at two body heights from up to four threats, straight-line reachable, and inside the future zone.",

  "Sight and fire tests ignore trees completely and sample a 1 m raster every 1 m, so canopy-hidden enemies are treated as visible and thin walls or corners can be misjudged.",
